title: Complete blood count: what the measurements describe
content: A complete blood count measures different types of blood cells. Hemoglobin is a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. White blood cells help the body fight infection. Platelets help blood form clots. Hematocrit describes the proportion of blood made up of red blood cells. A CBC result needs interpretation alongside other information about the person.

title: Cholesterol and lipid profile tests
content: A lipid profile measures fats in the blood, including cholesterol and triglycerides. Total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol and HDL cholesterol describe different parts of the lipid profile. Cholesterol has useful functions in the body. A clinician considers lipid results together with other health information.

title: Creatinine and kidney filtration
content: Creatinine is a waste product associated with muscle activity. The kidneys normally filter creatinine from the blood and remove it in urine. A creatinine test measures the amount in a blood or urine sample. A clinician may use creatinine along with other information to assess kidney function.

title: Liver panel measurements
content: A liver panel measures several substances in a blood sample. Albumin is a protein made by the liver. ALT, AST and ALP are enzymes measured in liver panels. Bilirubin is related to the breakdown of red blood cells. Several tests may be considered together when a clinician assesses liver health.

title: TSH and thyroid testing
content: TSH means thyroid stimulating hormone. A TSH test measures the amount of this hormone in the blood. Thyroid hormones affect how the body uses energy. A TSH result may need to be considered together with other thyroid tests.

title: HbA1c and blood glucose
content: Glucose is a sugar that cells use for energy. HbA1c is a blood test that reflects average blood glucose over the preceding few months. A clinician interprets HbA1c together with other information about the person.
